text.p: An earthquake measuring 5.7 on the Richter scale rocked Lijiang county in China's southwestern province of Yunnan on Wednesday, the official Xinhua news agency said.
Some houses collapsed and cracks had been found in many buildings in three impoverished villages in the area, but there were no reports of casualties, Xinhua said.
Lijiang was hit by a tremor measuring 7.0 on the Richter on February 3, killing at least 304 people and injuring more than 16,000.
"The quake happened at exactly the same spot as an earthquake in February," Xinhua said.
China is currently going through a period of intense seismological activity, Chinese experts say.
